newsitem.title: USA: U.S. municipal finance probe still open - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: U.S. municipal finance probe still open - WSJ.

text.p: Though the National Association of Securities Dealers has been investigating the municipal finance business for four years without charging any of the nation's largest bond underwriters, the probe is still active, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
Alden Adkins, general counsel of NASD regulation, is quoted as saying he expects "charges will be brought," though investigators have not contacted some of the firms involved for over a year.

The Securities and Exchange Commission, which is also pursuing an investigation, declined to comment in the Journal's story, though people close to the agency are cited as saying it is no longer developing cases.

The case began when the NASD and SEC found evidence that Armacon Securities of Clementon, N.J., was receiving payments from some of the nation's largest securities firms for work in municipal bond issues, the story says.
Regulators suspected that now-defunct Armacon was not doing any of the things it and the big securities firms said it was supposed to do, the story says.
As many as a dozen of the firms once being probed assume they've been exonerated, the story says.
